title: Two-phase drift monitoring and automatic retraining (TPDM-AR) for electric load forecasting
author: Oliveira, Silva

steps.title: Define monitoring configuration
steps.instruction: Define the hourly load series y(t); set forecasting design to use a 48‑hour input window and predict a 24‑hour horizon; select drift detectors ADWIN, KSWIN, and PH; set Phase‑2 smoothing window wMA = 24 samples; set consensus horizon S = 8 days.

steps.title: Prepare load series
steps.instruction: For synthetic validation generate hourly data for Jan–Mar 2024, keep Jan for training, Feb as drift‑free reference, and Mar for drift‑injected evaluation; for real‑data validation build y(t) from the UCI Global_active_power (kW) by parsing Date and Time, interpolate missing values by time interpolation, and resample to hourly mean active power; define the initial reference window ref as 7 consecutive days (Aug 1‑7) for later threshold calibration.

steps.title: Inject controlled drift
steps.instruction: In the synthetic March series inject incremental drift using linear and logarithmic distortion profiles that reach a final intensity p ∈ {10, 20, 30, 40, 50}% by day 31.

steps.title: Create sliding‑window samples
steps.instruction: Build supervised learning samples with sliding windows: inputs xi = (yi,…,yi+47) and targets zi = (yi+48,…,yi+71).

steps.title: Fit MinMax scaler
steps.instruction: Fit a MinMaxScaler on the baseline month only (synthetic: January 2024; real‑world: July 2007) for both inputs and outputs, then normalize all data to the [0,1] range to avoid leakage.

steps.title: Train MLP forecaster
steps.instruction: Train an MLPRegressor on the baseline month only (synthetic: January 2024; real‑world: July 2007), freeze the model, and keep detector hyper‑parameters fixed as given in the table‑based configuration.

steps.title: Run multi‑step forecasting
steps.instruction: At each forecast origin t produce a 24‑step ahead forecast y^{t+h|t} for h = 1…24. For the synthetic regime issue one 24‑step forecast per daily anchor (00:00) to obtain a single hourly forecast stream ŷ(t); unfold the horizon so that ŷ(t+h) = y^{t+h|t} and concatenate daily horizons. For the real‑data regime keep the per‑origin forecast vectors (origin hourly, Δt = 1 h) to compute the horizon‑aggregated error MAE24(t).

steps.title: Calculate raw errors
steps.instruction: Synthetic regime: compute pointwise absolute error ε(t) = |y(t) − ŷ(t)| on denormalized values. Real‑data regime: compute AEt+h|t = |y_{t+h} − y^{t+h|t}| and aggregate to MAE24(t) = (1/24) Σ_{h=1}^{24} AEt+h|t, yielding one scalar per forecast origin.

steps.title: Smooth error with moving average
steps.instruction: Apply a moving average of length wMA = 24 to the raw error stream (ε(t) for synthetic, MAE24(t) for real) to obtain the smoothed signal MA24(t). Use MA24(t) as the Phase 2 monitoring signal for the detectors.

steps.title: Set Phase‑2 threshold
steps.instruction: Synthetic regime: compute Tref = max_{t∈Feb} MA24(t) (February is drift‑free). Real‑data regime: compute Tref = max_{t∈ref} MAE24(t) where ref is the initial 7‑day window; use a fixed‑global Tref (detectors operate on smoothed MA24(t) but the threshold is based on the non‑smoothed values).

steps.title: Monitor raw load (Phase 1)
steps.instruction: Run ADWIN, KSWIN, and PH on the raw y(t) stream, logging any Phase 1 alerts (optionally include a Daily‑MAE curve for context).

steps.title: Monitor smoothed error (Phase 2)
steps.instruction: Run the same three detectors on MA24(t), log alert timestamps, and define the candidate consensus interval [t_i*, t_l*] from the first Phase 2 alert to the alert that completes three‑detector consensus.

steps.title: Apply Phase 2 confirmation rule
steps.instruction: Confirm degradation only if (i) three‑detector consensus occurs within horizon S = 8 days, and (ii) persistence holds: MA24(t) > Tref for every t in [t_i*, t_l*]; t_l* is the timestamp of the third detector’s first alert within the window S.

steps.title: Schedule retraining and restart
steps.instruction: If confirmed, define a retraining window [t_l* − 22 days, t_l* + 7 days]; after the +7‑day post‑consensus buffer, retrain the model on data in that window, deploy the updated model, re‑initialize all detectors for Phase 1 and Phase 2, use a new 7‑day reference week to set the Phase 2 baseline, and resume monitoring (re‑calibrate Tref if using a fixed‑global policy).

steps.title: Archive experiment artifacts
steps.instruction: Save configuration (all hyperparameters), timestamps of Phase 1 and Phase 2 alerts, error streams (MAE24(t), MA24(t)), validation metrics (MAE, MSE, RMSE), figures, and logs required to reproduce the exact runs.
